title: Snapshot-driven code review with a gated artifact report
objective: Measure the snapshot-review class under volume: read a staged change-set snapshot from the artifacts drawer, ground findings in the actual diff, catch every seeded defect, raise nothing against the constructs that only look like defects, and produce a severity-ranked, file-cited report artifact whose verdict follows from the findings.
prompt: A change-set snapshot for review rev-eval-1 is staged in this project's artifacts drawer: reviews/rev-eval-1/manifest.json and reviews/rev-eval-1/changes.diff. Run the code-review craftbook against it and write the gated report artifact to reviews/rev-eval-1/report.md with write_artifact. The diff is the change set under review; the matching source files are in the workspace, and docs/review-conventions.md is the house style this codebase is reviewed against. Also leave the machine-readable finding list at the workspace path review-output/findings.json with write_file - a JSON array with one record per finding, each record naming the file (the path as it appears in the diff), the line, a severity of critical, major, minor or nit, a category, and a recommendation - so the follow-up fix pass can pick it up. Do not change any source file: review-output/findings.json is the only workspace file you write.

setup.about: A small payments service. A seven-file change set is staged for review in the artifacts drawer; the house style it is reviewed against is documented in docs/review-conventions.md.

files.content:
# Review conventions

The house rules this codebase is reviewed against.

- Every SQL statement uses placeholders. A request value is never
  concatenated or interpolated into a query string.
- Every acquired resource (file handle, connection, lock) is released on
  every path out of the function, including the error path.
- A caught error is either handled or re-thrown. A catch block never
  reports success.
- Slice and range bounds are half-open: `slice(start, start + size)`.
- Debug logging does not ship.

## Deliberate patterns - correct as written

These three shapes look like common smells and are not. They are house
style, and a review must not raise them as findings.

- `== null` is the one loose comparison the style allows. It matches null
  and undefined together and nothing else, which is precisely what an
  optional field needs. It is not to be tightened to `===`.
- Best-effort background writes (audit, telemetry) are deliberately not
  awaited, so they cannot delay or break the request that triggered them.
  A `.catch` handler attached at the call site is the required form; a
  promise carrying a `.catch` is not a floating promise.
- Express selects error middleware by arity: a handler is only registered
  as an error handler when it declares exactly four parameters. The
  parameters such a handler does not use are required by that signature
  and stay.

success.summary: reviews/rev-eval-1/report.md exists in the artifacts drawer with Summary/Findings/Verdict sections, a severity table citing the flawed files, and a request-changes verdict; review-output/findings.json holds one record per finding carrying at least file, line, severity, category and recommendation (extra context such as a title or a cwe is welcome), lists every seeded defect (unparameterized SQL, the off-by-one page bound, the swallowed settings error, the leaked export file handle), repeats none of the three documented house-style smells, and raises nothing against the two files outside the change set.

checks.label: request-changes verdict (SQL concat is at least major)

requiredOutput.label: every seeded defect reported, and no correct-as-written construct reported

axes.name: grounding
axes.description: Findings reference code that actually appears in changes.diff; nothing is invented and cited lines exist.

axes.name: precision
axes.description: The three documented house-style constructs (the `== null` check, the unawaited best-effort audit write with its .catch, the four-parameter Express error handler) are not raised as findings, and the two files outside the change set (src/util.js, src/logger.js) carry no findings at all; if a house-style construct is discussed it is to clear it. A different, real defect found in one of those three files is good review work and counts in its favour, not against it.

axes.name: severity-judgment
axes.description: The SQL string concatenation, the off-by-one page bound, the swallowed settings error and the leaked export file handle are rated critical or major; the console.log and TODO are minor or nit - severities proportionate to impact.

axes.name: actionability
axes.description: Every finding carries a concrete, minimal recommendation (e.g. return to parameterized queries, close the handle in a finally), not generic advice.

axes.name: verdict-consistency
axes.description: The verdict follows mechanically from the findings table: any critical or major finding yields request-changes.

rubric.contextNote: The report is an artifacts-drawer file and review-output/findings.json is the single workspace file the reviewer writes - no source file may change. Some of the reviewed code only looks wrong: docs/review-conventions.md records which shapes are deliberate house style. src/util.js and src/logger.js are in the workspace as context but are not in the change set - manifest.json's seven files are.
